facts: One tall backing board is shown in slight perspective, with a visible narrow right edge and an oblique rectangular base.
Exactly two upright thermometers are mounted side by side, wet on the left and dry on the right.
Each thermometer has one upper and one lower horizontal retaining bracket, four brackets in total.
The long stems are almost parallel and the scale ladders occupy corresponding vertical ranges.
The slight offset of the paired thermometers follows the source perspective, not a new different calibration.
Both thermometers have rounded upper ends, narrow stems, lower bulbs and dark internal columns.
Dense horizontal graduation ladders flank each stem. The major long marks repeat over the same approximate range, with many smaller marks between them.
No readable numeric scale values, units, temperature reading or humidity value are printed.
The dark column on the left is lower than the one on the right in this illustrative state; do not convert the relative heights into numeric readings.
The right thermometer's lower bulb is exposed; it does not touch the water reservoir.
Only the left lower bulb has the irregular gauze covering.
A gauze strip descends from that covered bulb into a short open water reservoir directly beneath the left thermometer.
The reservoir has an elliptical open rim, short side walls and a rounded bottom, standing on the base.
The gauze/wick connects the wet bulb to the water; it is not a second thermometer stem, a disconnected cloth or a tube to the right bulb.
The source has no force, motion, airflow or operating-direction arrows.
